top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock is an original concept (removing the trap-induced shift while keeping many atoms in a Lamb-Dicke geometry) whose realisation delivered uncertainties near 1e-18, reproduced in several laboratories over about two decades. The two-name allocation to Katori and Ye maps onto idea and realisation, and a citation naming the magic-wavelength lattice states what is new relative to the 2005 and 2012 prizes. The remaining reservations (credit beyond the pair, instrument rather than discovery in nature) do not outweigh an award, so P001 ranks above no award.
